knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A child who can reach the water through an open gate stops water-side work. The learner keeps the child away from the water, tells the owner, and records the defect. Adjusting the latch or ignoring the defect is not acceptable.
A barrier check record shows what was seen, what was not inspected, and the defects found and who was told. It is not a certificate and does not show legal compliance.
A pool cover is not a barrier, even if locked. The learner records what is seen and escalates so that a barrier is considered.

practicalCriteria: Visual check record: on a supplied barrier scenario (site photographs or a walk-through), the learner records each item on the check sheet, marks any part not seen as not checked, and records gaps, gates, latches, climbable objects, doors, windows, locks and covers. The assessor checks each item against the scenario.

Escalation: for at least one supplied defect, the learner writes a defect report with location, time, observation and the person told, and states the next escalation step. The assessor checks that the owner and the business escalation contact are named.
Wording: the learner's record and any spoken summary contain no statement that the barrier complies, is certified or is approved. The assessor marks any such statement as a fail.
passRule: Knowledge checks: at least 2 of 3 correct (a reading result only, not verified practical competence). Practical sign-off is separate: assessor review of the visual check record, the escalation and the wording against the practical criteria.
evidenceRequired: Completed barrier check record and defect report, saved and dated
Assessor sign-off on the practical criteria
stopWorkCriteria: A child or an unsupervised person can reach the water through a barrier defect
The learner is asked to certify, sign or describe a barrier as compliant
The learner is asked to adjust a latch, hinge or self-closer, or repair a barrier outside the work order
A barrier defect is found and the owner has not been told
